Regional Commander Yuan Lisong of Taiyuan
translationRepairs: In the first year of Tangxi, the capital inspection was abolished and only the triennial completion review was used.
In the first year of Kangxi, the capital inspection was abolished and only the triennial completion review was used.

Wikisource preserves the same received graph 唐熙 as the chapter; there is no Tangxi era. After Shunzhi 17, the 元年/三年/六年 sequence is Kangxi, and the idiomatic already reads Kangxi, so the literal must be emended from Tangxi.
Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia strongly supported it, as did Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangdong.
Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia strongly supported it, as did Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangshu.
給事中魏象樞 names Wei Xiangshu; 樞 is shū, not dong. Xiangdong is a misromanization, and the proposed idiomatic line corrects only that name.
Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia strongly upheld it; Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangdong also requested it.
Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia strongly upheld it; Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangshu also requested it.
The literal likewise misreads 魏象樞 as Wei Xiangdong; Xiangshu matches 象樞, and the rest of the rendering already tracks 力主之 / 亦以為請.
An edict was received: impeaching officials who, following grand-assessment disposition, impeached falsely out of private motive would be punished.
An edict was received: officials who made supplementary impeachments would be punished according to grand-assessment rules if they impeached falsely out of private motive.

得旨，糾拾官照大計處分挾私妄糾者論 means supplementary-impeachment officials are punished by grand-assessment rules when they falsely impeach from private motive. The prior literal reverses and garbles that structure; the proposed wording restores it.
In Yongzheng 6 (1728), Regional Commander Yuan Lisong of Taiyuan memorialized that Garrison Commander Liang Yulian of Pingyuan was honest, capable, and skilled, yet was impeached for age.
In Yongzheng 6 (1728), Regional Commander Yuan Lisong of Taiyuan memorialized that Garrison Commander Liang Yu of Pingyuan was honest, keen, and skilled, yet was impeached for age.
平垣營守備梁玉廉潔敏練 names 梁玉; 廉潔敏練 are the descriptors honest, keen, and skilled. Liang Yulian wrongly absorbs 廉 into the personal name; keen better matches 敏.
In the sixth year, Taiyuan regional commander Yuan Lisong of Shanxi memorialized that Pingyuan garrison commander Liang Yulian was honest, keen, and skilled, yet was impeached on account of age.
In the sixth year, Taiyuan regional commander Yuan Lisong of Shanxi memorialized that Pingyuan garrison commander Liang Yu was honest, keen, and skilled, yet was impeached on account of age.
The literal has the same name-boundary error: 梁玉 is the person, and 廉潔敏練 are already rendered as honest, keen, and skilled. Changing only Yulian to Yu is correct.
